target.title: test(qa): migrate channel thread and DM isolation scenarios
target.body:
Closes #101111

## What Problem This Solves

Thread follow-up/isolation, reply override, subagent thread spawn, and direct-message session behavior were split across imperative Slack and Matrix scenario owners. That duplicated orchestration and made native relation evidence and cross-adapter parity harder to maintain.

## Why This Change Was Made

This migrates the parity-proven behavior family to six canonical YAML flows hosted by the shared scenario runner. Slack and Matrix adapters now expose the required stable normalized observations, including native thread/reply identifiers where available, and the replaced imperative owners and obsolete tests are removed rather than retained behind compatibility layers. Distinct Telegram and WhatsApp scenarios remain where their behavior is not exact parity.

## User Impact

No production channel behavior, routing, commands, restart/config surface, or infrastructure changes. QA ownership becomes canonical and shared across adapters, with less duplicated scenario code and clearer native relation evidence.

## Evidence

- Exact pushed head: `3a01650fd197c31aab153437c8a5885013900ace`.
- Focused exact-head Testbox proof: 9 files / 208 tests passed across QA Lab and Matrix.
- Full project `tsgo` typecheck passed before a conflict-free rebase onto current `origin/main`; focused exact-head tests passed after the rebase.
- qa-channel `thread-follow-up` and `thread-isolation` passed: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/suite-mr9jlf2y-a24d200a/qa-suite-report.md`.
- Matrix Crabline `thread-follow-up` and `thread-isolation` passed with native relation evidence: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/suite-mr9jlsag-934ec4cd/qa-suite-report.md`.
- Matrix live thread reply override passed.
- Matrix live shared-DM passed: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/suite-mr9ijndt-1b96c71f/qa-suite-report.md`.
- Matrix live per-room DM passed: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/suite-mr9ikpna-ab6f4a58/qa-suite-report.md`.
- Telegram Crabline relation proof is inapplicable because its fake API does not echo `message_thread_id`; Matrix is the applicable bridge used here.
- Rebased onto `origin/main` after #101063 landed; conflict resolution preserves its Matrix observer runtime identity bridge. Exact rebased lint plus 205 focused tests passed, and final full-branch autoreview is clean. The broad coverage-report test still fails for the same four sibling restart/policy taxonomy IDs on current `origin/main`; this branch adds no unknown coverage IDs.
- Corrected-head CI exposed one rebase-only prod type failure: the canonical Slack adapter's existing internal facade omitted `listSlackThreadMessages`. The helper export is restored; remote prod `tsgo`, bundled extension lint, 41 Slack tests, and a clean focused autoreview passed.
- QA Smoke on `b47b2c9db1f2cc092d17b63c0492a27b1858ffd5` selected `thread-follow-up` and `thread-isolation` through the implicit Telegram Crabline profile. The migration had dropped their existing `requiredChannelDriver: qa-channel` pin, while the fake Telegram provider cannot echo the native topic relation. The pin and catalog/profile coverage are restored.
- QA Smoke correction proof on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwweyngd49d4wmgkj15ffp5z`: targeted QA Lab tests passed 147/147; explicit qa-channel thread flows passed 2/2; the exact packaged `smoke-ci` command passed in 8m59s.
- Fresh Codex autoreview of the QA Smoke correction completed clean with no accepted/actionable findings (confidence 0.86).
- Known bounded gap: Matrix emitted the native subagent `session active` thread intro immediately on both attempts, but the child completion did not arrive before either 360-second hard timeout.
- AI-assisted implementation; no transcript attached.
